To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the SagDEG stream can contribute to the galactic dark matter halo; (ii) the annual modulation signal due to the stream can be of the right size and phase to account for the DAMA/NAI annual modulation signal; (iii) the annual modulation due to the stream is not affected by any other astrophysical source of modulation, such as e.g., the Earth motion with respect to the galactic gravitational potential, the Earth orbital motion around the Sun,

1) the SagDEG contribution to the galactocentric dark halo is not able to reproduce the DAMA/NAI data; 2) the SagDEGs contribution to the solar neighborhood dark halo is not sufficient to explain the DAMA/ NaI results, but it is not excluded by them; 3) the SagDEGS contribution to the galatic halo is compatible with the DAMA/ NAIs results only in some specific cases, but it is excluded in others

(i) the SagDEG dark matter stream contribution can account for the DAMA/ NaI annual modulation signature in the case of some WIMP candidates, and for some of the astrophic, nuclear and particle physic scenarios.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the possible signatures of the SagDEGs dark matter contribution to the galatic halo in terms of annual modulation of the rate.
the investigation of possible signatures of the presence of non-thermalized dark matter substructures, in order to contribute to the knowledge of the galactic halo.
the investigation of the possible signatures of the SagDEGs dark matter stream in the DAMA/ NaI annual modulation signal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DAMA/NAI annual modulation data can be compatible with a WIMP signal in the presence of the SagDEGG dark matter substructure.
the DAMA/NAI annual modulation signal is not in contrast with the presence of SagDEG dark matter substructures.

, on the basis of our present knowledge, it is not possible to exclude the presence of a dark matter stream in the halo of the Milky way, which is compatible with the DAMA/NAI annual modulation data, and, at the same time, compatible with the other experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of the WIMP candidates considered, the SagDEG stream contribution to the dark matter halo of the Milky way is compatible with the DAMA/NAI annual modulation results.

the present study suggests a non-excluded possibility of the SagDEGs dark matter stream contribution as the source of the annual modulation signal observed by DAMA/NaIs experiment, but it does not allow to draw any firm conclusions.

the annual modulation effect is not a unique signature of the DAMA/LIBRA and DAMA/NaIs results, but it can be a consequence of the presence in the halo of non-thermalized structures such as streams, and it could be also a consequence of some other astrophysical, cosmological or nuclear scenarios.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of a dark matter stream in the Milky Way halo can produce an annual modulation signature in the direction of the Earth orbit, even in the absence of a galactic wind and/or of a dark matter halo density gradient.
a dark matter substructure such as SagDEG can contribute to the annual modulation signature in a model independent way.
the SagDEG stream contribution can be a possible explanation of the DAMA/LIBRA annual modulation signal.
